NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, 2521 and 2530 due to the continuing state of emergency,
  including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID -19 virus, this
  meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person in the
  Council Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling 1-669-900-6833 from any phone, Meeting
  ID: 875 6711 3695, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
  the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 875 6711 3695, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 11, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), due to the continuing state
of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of
the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by two unnamed members of the public.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

**ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Initiation of litigation: one potential case

City Attorney Davis reported out the following actions from the closed session:

  CITY COUNCIL DIRECTED THE CITY ATTORNEY’S OFFICE TO ISSUE A
  NOTICE OF VIOLATION TO STOLZ MANAGEMENT AND THE
  PROMENADE, LLC, STATING THAT THEY ARE IN VIOLATION OF THEIR
  ENTITLEMENTS REQUIRING THEM TO MAINTAIN A SHARED PARKING
  AGREEMENT WITH THE NORRIS THEATER IN FULL FORCE AND
  EFFECT AT ALL TIMES, ORDERING THEM TO CEASE THE CONDUCT
  PROHIBITING PARKING OF THEATER EVENTS AS REQUIRED BY THAT
  AGREEMENT, AND REQUIRING THEM TO COMPLY WITHIN A VERY
  SHORT PERIOD OF TIME. IF STOLZ AND THE PROMENADE, LLC DO NOT
  COMPLY WITH THE CITY’S NOTICE, DIRECTED THE CITY ATTORNEY’S
  OFFICE TO FILE A CIVIL ACTION IN COURT TO COMPEL THEM BY
  OBTAINING A COURT ORDER.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 11, 2022
 **ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment related to the Promenade and the Palos Verdes Performing Arts (PVPA) was
received by: Claire Kresser, Paige Gormley, Grace Moulton, Jen Clinton, Gabi Ryan, Brenda
Bilstad, Damon Aldrich and Christina Stockhausen.

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING  OCTOBER  2022  "BREAST  CANCER
  AWARENESS MONTH"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared October 2022 “Breast Cancer Awareness Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF OCTOBER 2022

  APPROVED WARRANTS 65576 THROUGH 65599 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $341,909.79 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090622 THROUGH
  090722; IN THE AMOUNT OF $85,710.51 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $427,620.30 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 6, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 19,
  2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  REQUEST TO AWARD A PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO KORMEX
  CONSTRUCTION, INC. FOR THE ERNIE HOWLETT PARK PERIMETER PATHWAY
  PROJECT

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 11, 2022
   Recommendation: That City Council 1.) Accept the bid from Kormex Construction,
  Inc. in the amount of $319,650, plus a 15% contingency ($47,947) for a grand total of
  $367,597; 2.) Approve the Public Works contract between the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates and Kormex Construction, Inc. to the satisfaction of the City Attorney; and 3.)
  Authorize a Fiscal Year 2022-23 budget adjustment in the amount of $177,577 from
  Park Facilities Fees toward the project.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Management Analyst Slawson explained that the project was approved in 2012 and the grant
was awarded to the City in 2013-14, but due to transitions in staffing and the COVID-19
pandemic, the project was put on hold. She further explained that staff was able to maintain
the grant during that time, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

Management Analyst Slawson explained there will be wayfinding signage throughout the
perimeter pathway, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA. COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHMITZ further explained that the exercise equipment locations were chosen to encourage
walking between stations, while also not interfering with any ball play or sports happening
throughout the park.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1.) ACCEPT THE BID FROM KORMEX CONSTRUCTION, INC. IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $319,650, PLUS A 15% CONTINGENCY ($47,947) FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL OF $367,597; 2.) APPROVE THE PUBLIC WORKS
  CONTRACT BETWEEN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND
  KORMEX CONSTRUCTION, INC. TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY; AND 3.) AUTHORIZE A FISCAL YEAR 2022-23 BUDGET
  ADJUSTMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $177,577 FROM PARK FACILITIES
  FEES TOWARD THE PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  SECOND AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Second Amendment to City
  Manager Employment Agreement and authorize its execution by the Mayor.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR ZERUNYAN praised City Manager Grammer for his leadership and thanked him for
his service to the City Council and the community.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER
  EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZE ITS EXECUTION BY THE
  MAYOR.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 11, 2022
 9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF PROPOSED ORDINANCE NO. 744
  AMENDING THE MUNICIPAL CODE REGARDING: (1) AN UPDATE TO CHAPTER
  17.76 (DENSITY BONUS AND OTHER INCENTIVES), (2) AMENDMENTS TO
  CHAPTER 17.30 (COMMERCIAL-GENERAL DISTRICT) TO PROVIDE FOR BONUS
  LEVEL DEVELOPMENT, AND (3) A NEW CHAPTER 17.82 (DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENTS); AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2531 APPROVING A LIST
  OF COMMUNITY AMENITIES AND BENEFITS THAT MAY BE PROVIDED FOR
  BONUS LEVEL DEVELOPMENT UNDER MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 17.30
  (COMMERCIAL-GENERAL DISTRICT)

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) adopt Ordinance No. 744; and (2) adopt
  Resolution No. 2531 establishing a list of approved community amenities and benefits
  for consideration in exchange for bonus level development under RHEMC Chapter
  17.30, as amended by Ordinance No. 744.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN stated that he feels including art in the Resolution is
problematic and subjective. Discussion ensued about the inclusion of art.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 744.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2531 ESTABLISHING A LIST OF APPROVED
  COMMUNITY AMENITIES AND BENEFITS FOR CONSIDERATION IN
  EXCHANGE FOR BONUS LEVEL DEVELOPMENT UNDER RHEMC
  CHAPTER 17.30, AS AMENDED BY ORDINANCE NO. 744.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that Los Angeles County continues to be in the low
transmission level. He added that the updated booster shots are available for those 12 years
and older.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF attended a Holiday Parade Subcommittee meeting earlier that
evening with COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, and it was decided that the annual Holiday
Parade of Lights’ Hometown Grand Marshal will be COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN. The
parade will be held on December 3 at 6:00 P.M.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 11, 2022
 MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also reported that the Tracy Austin Tennis Tournament will be held
this weekend at the Jack Kramer Club and at Ernie Howlett Park.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also reported that the Neighborhood Watch meeting would be held
next Tuesday, October 18 at 6:00 P.M. via Zoom.

Lastly, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF attended the Oktoberfest event held by the Palos Verdes
Library District on October 1.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEVE ZUCKERMAN thanked the Holiday Parade Subcommittee for the
honor of being named the Parade Hometown Grand Marshal.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that yesterday was National Indigenous Peoples Day,
and acknowledged that the City of Rolling Hills Estates is on Gabrielino-Tongva land, as noted
in the General Plan.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:17 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Council
Member Stegura’s niece, Oklahoma City Sgt. Meagan Burke. The meeting was adjourned
to Tuesday, October 25, 2022, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 11, 2022
